When does a person lose their right to privacy and to be forgotten?

A person in the public eye only has a right to a modicum of privacy, and it should be applicable only to medical files. Politicians should have publicly viewable (or at least publicly requestable) pay, bank accounts, taxes, etc. If for nothing else than to attempt to keep them honest. Long shot, but worth one.

Other than that, a private citizen (I.e. John Doe down the street, not John Beohner) should be afforded much more privacy. Anything publicly available is fair game, though, still.

A public figure, as is a politician has no right to privacy in some circumstances - you can't demand to enter his house on these grounds but he also can't refuse to answer some questions, like Bill Clinton had to.
If you hold or have ever held a position of authority over other people you should be the only one to lose this right. This includes business leaders and government bureaucrats.

Having privacy as a right sounds nice, but the reality is that you lose it the moment you stop protecting it. These politicians keep their secrets because they bury them. It's not like we're all just waiting on a court order to see the dirt.

They burn evidence, pay people off, or threaten them, or kill them.

You earn privacy by removing the ability of others to take it away from you. You don't ask for it nicely.
